Key observations: rotted taproot/stem at soil line with distinctive **blue-green spore masses** on the tissue, dark decay, dead plant material. The blue-green coloration on roots is highly characteristic of Sudden Death Syndrome.

Let me check reference images to confirm.
The SDS reference image (bottom-left) shows a rotted taproot with blue coloration that closely matches the test image. Let me check a few more to be thorough.
Neither Phytophthora nor Rhizoctonia show blue-green spores. Let me check two more for completeness.

Charcoal Rot shows black microsclerotia (no blue-green), Brown Stem Rot shows internal browning. Neither matches.

**Conclusion:** The test image shows a severely rotted taproot with distinctive **blue-green spore masses** on the tissue. This is the hallmark diagnostic feature of Sudden Death Syndrome — the SDS pathogen (*Fusarium virguliforme*) produces blue-green spores visible on taproots, especially after rain. The SDS reference collage (bottom-left panel) shows an almost identical image. No other class produces this blue-green coloration on roots.
